name: Over-commit and pay
citation: library/mk2/arcade.frames.json: mileena/roll/gap_px 192 -> on_block -34, damage 21, knockdown 1. mileena/teleport_kick/gap_px 192 -> on_hit -5, on_block -25, damage 32. reptile/HK/far -> damage 32, connect_range 110.
claim: The two biggest commitments in Mileena's kit, blocked. The roll is -34 and pays for it: Reptile blocks, counters, and lands 32 through her guard. The teleport kick is -25 and gets away with it -- because the blocked teleport always leaves a 153 px gap and nothing Reptile owns reaches past 110. A negative number is not a verdict.

beats.name: roll-blocked
beats.note: roll = back . back . down . HK, the profile's own special_inputs encoding played with 2 neutral frames between steps (a direction chorded with its trigger does not register). Contact f33, 5 chip. She guards from f19.

beats.name: roll-punished
beats.note: Reptile drops guard at contact+1 and counters at his earliest actionable frame (global f56 = contact+23). 32 damage on a Mileena who has held Block since f19.

beats.name: teleport-blocked
beats.note: teleport_kick = forward . forward . LK. Contact f132, 4 chip. The blocked teleport lands Mileena at a FIXED distance: every rung from 61 px to 192 px ends at a 153 px gap (measured, 6 rungs).

beats.name: punish-refused-by-range
beats.note: The same punish program that collected 32 damage off the roll. -25 and it reaches NOTHING: the gap is 151 px and Reptile's longest connect range is 110 px (far HK / far LK). docs/frames.md 1, the range clause.

notes: Rung: m-gap-0 (gap_px 192) -- the rung both specials were measured at. mk2.md refuses roll/teleport rows at any other gap because both moves make x discontinuous.
refusals: The brief's 'blocked teleport_kick -> punished again' is REFUSED. Reason: RANGE. The blocked teleport leaves a 153 px gap from every starting rung measured (192/146/114/99/83/71 px all end at 153 px); no Reptile move in arcade.frames.json has a connect_range above 110. The beat is kept as an empirically executed NON-punish rather than dropped, because the refusal is the lesson.
